text:
mira_ops: FYI - after the BMC microcode push to eu-west-1 last night we have ~30 GPU nodes stuck in provisioning. Observed boot path switching to iGPU via BMC, so the GPU isn't initialized. TPM logs show a boot policy flip.

alex_m: seeing a jump in failed provisioning in the metrics too (provisioner.retries x5). Suspect the new micro toggles the BIOS MUX on certain SKUs.

samir: can you paste the logs from one affected host?

mira_ops: sure - sample from host gpu-eu1-023:```
[    1.234567] tpm_tis 00:0a: 1.2.3 TPM: Boot policy event: 0x14 -> 0x1
[    1.234580] ACPI: EC: Boot-order override detected
[    2.456700] pci 0000:01:00.0: firmware: failed to initialize GPU, device disabled
IPMI SEL: 0x20 Power overridden by BMC, bootdev=pxe->disk
```

mira_ops: ipmitool output shows boot order toggled by BMC script:```
# ipmitool fru|grep -i bmc
Board Mfg: AcmeOEM
# ipmitool raw 0x3a 0x0f 0x01
0x01 0x00 0x01 0x02
```

tess: runbook check - there is a known vendor micro that enables "auto-boot-mux" for power-saver profiles. We usually force BIOS mux=discrete during provisioning. If BMC flips it on reboot the node comes up without GPU and the pxe hooks fail.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-334455 created (severity: high) — linked to provisioning surge.

alex_m: plan proposal: canary 5 nodes in eu-west-1b -> apply ipmitool raw to set MUX=discrete, cold power cycle via BMC, then retry provisioning job p-12345. If green, roll to remaining impacted hosts. We should avoid firmware rollback unless necessary.

samir: agree. Also we need a throttle in the provisioner to avoid double-requeueing jobs while nodes flap. Right now each failed deploy re-enqueues causing extra GPU-hours and billing spike. Estimated extra GPU-hours = 240 in last 6h (~$7.2k).

tess: I'll open a provisioner patch to add exponential backoff + a 10m global throttle for this incident. Canary at 10:30 UTC?

mira_ops: starting canary now on 5 nodes (gpu-eu1-021..025). Command used: ```for n in {21..25}; do ipmitool -H $n -U admin -P **** raw 0x30 0x45 0x01; ipmitool -H $n -U admin -P **** chassis power cycle; done```

mira_ops: canary results: 4/5 came up with GPU initialized, one node still booted without GPU (bios logged mux revert). I manually forced mux via vendor-bmcctl and reprovisioned; success.

alex_m: good. Next steps: 1) throttle provisioner (tess) 2) vendor engagement for micro rollback plan (mira) 3) schedule staged BMC config push to set persistent mux=discrete for impacted firmware versions (samir + infra runbook).

mira_ops: vendor response: they acknowledge change in 2.4.7 micro enabling auto-mux for thermal profiles. Rollback ETA 8h with staged rollout. They also provided a BMC raw command to disable auto-mux remotely if we script it (we tested on canary).

tess: temporary mitigation accepted: global provisioner throttle + targeted mux override during boots. I'll push the throttle in 15m.

samir: adding a quick metric alert: if provisioning failures > 10/min then pause automatic requeue and route jobs to Dedicated pool. Can someone tag @product if this will impact SLAs?

mira_ops: pinging product in #product for SLA note. For cost: we throttled requeues and moved 120 pending jobs to Dedicated, expected ramp cost ~+$3.5k/day vs current spike. Cheaper than repeated requeues.

oncall-bot: Update: Incident INC-2026-334455 severity maintained. Actions logged: canary, throttle, vendor rollback scheduled.

alex_m: keep monitoring. If vendor rollback slips we need an automated BMC config job to force mux state across fleet during boot (idempotent). I'll draft a safe-runbook for that.

mira_ops: will run a fleet query tonight to list firmware versions and flag nodes with micro >= 2.4.7. Posting CSV to the incident ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:
